source_caption:
How High (2001) is a stoner comedy starring Method Man and Redman as two underachieving friends, Silas and Jamal. After smoking some magically enhanced weed, they discover it helps them ace an important test, which lands them admission to Harvard University. Once there, they struggle to fit into the elite academic environment, often clashing with strict professors and rich students while using their unusual advantage to survive exams and challenges.

As the story unfolds, their wild behavior creates chaos on campus, but they also end up exposing hypocrisy and rigid systems within the university. The film mixes absurd humor, weed culture, and a bit of social commentary, highlighting themes of friendship and breaking stereotypes. Though it received mixed reviews, How High became a cult classic, especially among fans of early 2000s hip-hop culture and comedy films.

source_details.synopsis: How High is a 2001 American stoner comedy film directed by Jesse Dylan in his feature directorial debut and written by Dustin Lee Abraham. The film stars Method Man and Redman as two cannabis users who gain admission to Harvard University with the supernatural help of a deceased friend whose ashes were used to fertilize a marijuana plant. Obba Babatundé, Mike Epps, Jeffrey Jones, and Fred Willard also appear in supporting roles. Produced by Jersey Films and Native Pictures and distributed by Universal Pictures, How High was released on December 21, 2001. The film received generally negative reviews from critics, but later gained a cult following. A television sequel, How High 2, was released
